item.title: Rivers in the sky are raining down on the Pacific Northwest. What are they?
item.description: Atmospheric rivers are large bands of water vapor in the sky. They are dumping trillions of gallons of water on Washington and Oregon, just as high tides and winds batter shorelines.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Why even a fraction of a degree can escalate climate change impacts
item.description: Countries are not meeting their goal of limiting climate change to 1.5 degrees Celsius. How much hotter the planet gets makes a profound difference for the impacts the world could see.

item.title: Turkey hosts world climate summit, but some critics accuse it of 'greenwashing'
item.description: Thousands of diplomats, executives and leaders are gathering in Turkey for a global climate summit. In recent years, Turkey has moved to be more eco-conscious, but some say that hasn't been enough.

item.title: U.N. climate talks begin today. Here are 3 things to know
item.description: Countries are gathering in Antalya, Turkey, for the annual U.N. climate conference. Many are frustrated with the lack of focus on fossil fuels, the main driver of climate change.

item.title: COP31 starts Monday. As global temperatures continue to rise, do climate talks matter?
item.description: COP31 - the annual UN negotiations on climate change - starts on Monday. The talks have been going on for decades, during which the planet has gotten hotter. So, do these climate talks really matter?

item.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces
item.description: In October 2025, the remnants of a typhoon seriously damaged Alaska Native villages in the far western part of the state. A year later, one of the hardest hit communities is still recovering.
